findings.first_evidence: docs/agent-profiles.md:8 -- On Linux or macOS, create `agent-profiles.json` in the bridge's state directory
findings.suggested_fix: Expand the configuration instructions to distinguish standalone stateDir (HERDR_WEB_STATE_DIR, XDG_CONFIG_HOME or ~/.config/herdr-web-ui) from app-managed SSH bridges, whose catalog belongs at ~/.config/herdr-web-ui/bridges/<socket-sha256>.json.state/agent-profiles.json. Explain that the matching bridges/<hash>.json descriptor identifies the selected herdr socket via socket_path; do not display its token. Reopening the dialog rereads the catalog.
findings.title: Document the managed remote bridge catalog directory
findings.why_it_matters: Users configuring an app-managed SSH PC cannot discover its profiles by following the documented default path. Managed remote bridges pass a socket-specific state directory to createServer, so a catalog placed at ~/.config/herdr-web-ui/agent-profiles.json is silently treated as absent on that PC. Document the managed remote path and how to identify the descriptor for the chosen herdr socket, while preserving the standalone-server instructions.
findings.validation_reason: For an app-managed SSH PC configured at the newly documented default, docs/agent-profiles.md:8-9 directs the catalog to ~/.config/herdr-web-ui, but the reachable SSH launcher in server/remote-host.ts:130 runs remote-entry.ts, whose line 98 passes descriptor+'.state' from bridge.ts:10-15, and agent-profiles.ts:21-22 reads only that directory and treats the documented placement as absent; this new documentation defect is established by the caller chain, while user incidence was not measured.

findings.suggested_fix: Add focused launcher tests using stubbed herdr RPC responses: active agent at first check, missing/foreign foreground ownership, and an initially available shell becoming busy at the second check. Call startAgentProfile with a short timeout and assert agent_pane_busy plus zero pane.send_text calls; retain the existing successful wrapper contract tests.
findings.title: Test launch refusal before any terminal input
findings.why_it_matters: The new launcher writes an executable command into a terminal, so refusing a busy or unreadable foreground job is a consequential safety contract. Current tests exercise only availableProfileShell in isolation; the HTTP startup tests cover successful and blocked-after-execution launches, so bypassing the pre-write checks would leave the suite green. Exercise startAgentProfile with an active agent, unavailable foreground ownership and a ready-to-busy transition, asserting agent_pane_busy and no pane.send_text.
findings.validation_reason: The new safety gate in server/shell-agent.ts:118-135 needs an active agent, unreadable/foreign foreground ownership, or a ready-to-busy transition before paneSendText; inspected repository tests cover only availableProfileShell directly at shell-agent.test.ts:78-88 and successful or already-executed blocked launches at agent-profiles.contract.test.ts:46-146, with no startAgentProfile refusal test asserting agent_pane_busy and zero terminal writes, confirming the claimed regression coverage gap without alleging a demonstrated runtime bypass; incidence of these startup states was not measured.
